notation.text: The ambient space is real Euclidean space; the sphere carries its induced metric and usual stereographic smooth structure. The configuration has one sphere coordinate for each element of \(\operatorname{Fin}N\). The measure is fixed by Euclidean volume, not supplied arbitrarily.
notation.formula: E=\mathbb R^{n+1},\quad S=\{z\in E:\|z\|=1\},\quad M=S^{\operatorname{Fin}N},\quad \tau=\operatorname{vol}_E.\mathrm{toSphere},\quad \sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\tau,\quad\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}.

notation.text: This is the specified canonical radial extension of a sphere function with values in a real normed space. Its zero value at the origin totalizes the function. Derivatives defining sphere operators are taken at unit vectors, inside the open nonzero region.

The projection is onto the actual tangent hyperplane. The gradient uses the Euclidean Riesz representative of the radial differential. For a tangent C¹ field, the displayed divergence equals the intrinsic divergence: its radial differential agrees with the sphere differential, kills the normal, and has the same trace as the induced tangent endomorphism. This interpretation of divergence requires tangency.

Write \(x[i\leftarrow y]\) for replacement of coordinate \(i\) by \(y\). Differentiate that sphere coordinate while holding every other coordinate fixed. The pairing and divergence are sums, with no factor \(1/N\).

conventions: Each integral uses \(\mu\); all sums run over \(\operatorname{Fin}N\). There is no empirical averaging factor.
The measure inverse is taken in the nonnegative extended reals. Its finite positive denominator is established before normalization is used.
units.source_history_boundary: The source is the pinned generic geometric supplement. Historical single-sphere C² radial work is recorded in the reuse capsule; it does not by itself establish the C¹ finite-product result.

units.title: Weighted gradient integration by parts on product spheres
units.statement: For arbitrary \(n,N\in\mathbb N\), use \(E=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), its unit sphere \(S\), \(M=S^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\), the induced product smooth and metric structures, and the exact normalized polar product measure \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\) defined below. For every real \(f,\rho\in C^1(M)\) and \(g\in C^2(M)\), define the actual tangent field \(V_i=\rho\nabla_i g\). Then the three displayed integrands are integrable, its divergence has zero integral, and the weighted integration-by-parts identity holds. The field regularity and tangency are derived from these hypotheses. The weight \(\rho\) has no sign or normalization restriction.

assumptions: \(n,N\in\mathbb N\) are arbitrary, with no positivity restriction. Thus the ambient dimension is \(n+1\); \(n=0\) gives the two-point sphere and \(N=0\) gives a one-point empty product.

The scalar field is \(\mathbb R\). All norms, inner products, tangent projections and manifold metrics are induced by the Euclidean structure. Regularity means regularity in the usual stereographic sphere charts and their finite product charts.

The reference measure is exactly \(\mu=\sigma^{\otimes N}\), with \(\sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\tau\) and \(\tau=\operatorname{vol}_E.\mathrm{toSphere}\). Its finite nonzero mass and probability normalization are proved internally; they are not extra inputs.
For every \(f,\rho,g:M\to\mathbb R\), assume \(f,\rho\in C^1(M)\) and \(g\in C^2(M)\), jointly in all configuration coordinates.

The field is defined by \(V_i(x)=\rho(x)\nabla_i g(x)\). Its C¹ regularity and pointwise tangency are derived. No sign, strict positivity, normalization, or density interpretation is assumed for \(\rho\).

steps.title: Differentiate the joint radial extension
steps.text: Normalize every ambient coordinate on the open set where none is zero. Intrinsic C² regularity of \(g\) gives C² regularity of the joint radial extension there. Its full Fréchet derivative is C¹; composing with the configuration inclusion preserves this regularity. Restriction to the fixed linear insertion \(\iota_i:E\to E^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\) in coordinate \(i\) is the derivative of the sphere section \(g_{i,x}(y)=g(x[i\leftarrow y])\).
steps.formula: \widetilde g(z)=g\bigl((z_j/\|z_j\|)_j\bigr),\quad D\widetilde g|_M\in C^1,\quad D(g_{i,x}^{\mathrm r})(x_i)=D\widetilde g(x)\circ\iota_i,
steps.lean:
private theorem contMDiff_configurationRadial_fderiv {n N : ℕ}
    (g : SphereConfiguration n N → ℝ)
    (hg : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 2 g) :
    ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N)
      𝓘(ℝ, (Fin N → SphereAmbient n) →L[ℝ] ℝ) 1
      (fun x : SphereConfiguration n N =>
        fderiv ℝ (configurationRadialExtension g) (fun j => (x j : SphereAmbient n))) := by
  intro x
  have hd : ContDiffAt ℝ 1 (fderiv ℝ (configurationRadialExtension g))
      (fun j => (x j : SphereAmbient n)) :=
    (contDiffAt_configurationRadialExtension g hg (fun j => (x j : SphereAmbient n))
      (fun j => ne_zero_of_mem_unit_sphere (x j))).fderiv_right (by norm_num)
  exact hd.contMDiffAt.comp x (contMDiff_sphereConfiguration_coe 1 x)

steps.title: Recover a jointly C¹ tangent gradient
steps.text: Apply the fixed real Riesz inverse to the coordinate derivative, obtaining a jointly C¹ ambient vector \(G_i(x)\). The projection \(P_{x_i}\) depends smoothly on \(x_i\) through its explicit inner-product formula. Thus the actual coordinate tangent gradient is C¹ in the complete configuration, not just separately differentiable.
steps.formula: G_i(x)=\mathcal R^{-1}\bigl(D\widetilde g(x)\circ\iota_i\bigr),\qquad\nabla_i g(x)=G_i(x)-\langle x_i,G_i(x)\rangle x_i,\qquad\nabla_i g\in C^1(M;E).
steps.lean:
private theorem contMDiff_sphereProductGradient {n N : ℕ}
    (g : SphereConfiguration n N → ℝ)
    (hg : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 2 g) (i : Fin N) :
    ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1
      (fun x => sphereProductGradient g i x) := by
  let G : SphereConfiguration n N → SphereAmbient n := fun x =>
    (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (SphereAmbient n)).symm
      ((fderiv ℝ (configurationRadialExtension g) (fun j => (x j : SphereAmbient n))).comp
        (coordinateInsertion i))
  have hP : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n →L[ℝ] ℝ) 1
      (fun x : SphereConfiguration n N => (fderiv ℝ (configurationRadialExtension g)
        (fun j => (x j : SphereAmbient n))).comp (coordinateInsertion i)) :=
    (contMDiff_configurationRadial_fderiv g hg).clm_comp contMDiff_const
  have hG : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 G :=
    (InnerProductSpace.toDual ℝ (SphereAmbient n)).symm.toContinuousLinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearMap.contMDiff.comp hP
  have hx : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1
      (fun x : SphereConfiguration n N => (x i : SphereAmbient n)) :=
    contMDiff_pi_space.mp (contMDiff_sphereConfiguration_coe 1) i
  have hi : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 1
      (fun x => inner ℝ (x i : SphereAmbient n) (G x)) :=
    ((innerSL ℝ).contMDiff.comp hx).clm_apply hG
  have heq : (fun x => sphereProductGradient g i x) =
      fun x : SphereConfiguration n N => G x - inner ℝ (x i : SphereAmbient n) (G x) • (x i : SphereAmbient n) := by
    funext x
    unfold sphereProductGradient sphereTangentGradient gradient
    rw [configurationRadialExtension_section_fderiv g (hg.of_le (by norm_num)) x i,
      Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val, Submodule.starProjection_singleton]
    simp only [norm_eq_of_mem_sphere, one_pow, RCLike.ofReal_one, div_one]
    rfl
  rw [heq]
  exact hG.sub (hi.smul hx)

steps.title: Construct the weighted tangent field
steps.text: Multiply by the supplied C¹ scalar weight. Product regularity gives C¹ components, and orthogonal projection gives tangency at every point. Neither argument uses a sign or a normalization condition on the weight.
steps.formula: V_i(x)=\rho(x)\nabla_i g(x),\qquad V_i\in C^1(M;E),\qquad\langle x_i,V_i(x)\rangle=\rho(x)\langle x_i,\nabla_i g(x)\rangle=0.
steps.lean:
have hV (i : Fin N) : ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1
      (fun x => rho x • sphereProductGradient g i x) :=
    hrho.smul (contMDiff_sphereProductGradient g hg i)
  have hT (x : SphereConfiguration n N) (i : Fin N) :
      inner ℝ (x i : SphereAmbient n) (rho x • sphereProductGradient g i x) = 0 := by
    rw [inner_smul_right]
    have ht : inner ℝ (x i : SphereAmbient n) (sphereProductGradient g i x) = 0 :=
      tangentGradient_tangent (fun y => g (Function.update x i y)) (x i)
    rw [ht, mul_zero]

steps.title: Substitute into the proved product identity
steps.text: Apply the preceding finite-product theorem to this actual field. Move the real scalar weight through the inner product and finite sum. This gives the two identities and integrability of each displayed integrand. The preceding theorem and its reviewed supporting lemmas provide the normalization, intrinsic differential identification, annular transport and finite-product steps P1–P4; these are reused proof results, not new premises.
steps.lean:
have h := sphere_product_tangential_integration_by_parts f
    (fun i x => rho x • sphereProductGradient g i x) hf hV hT
  simpa only [inner_smul_right, Finset.mul_sum] using h

units.lean_statement: The type quantifies n and N first, then f, rho and g. It assumes C¹ f, C¹ rho and C² g and defines V locally in the conclusion. It does not assume C¹ regularity or tangency of that derived field.
units.lean_proof: The full product radial extension yields a jointly C¹ derivative field. Riesz representation and the explicit orthogonal projection produce a C¹ tangent gradient. The proof then invokes the main finite-product theorem and rewrites the finite pairing.
units.dependency_notes: The preceding product-sphere integration-by-parts theorem supplies the integral conclusions. Its reviewed supporting lemmas establish measure normalization and actual differential/trace identification; the annular divergence and product Fubini arguments support its proof. This specialization derives its vector-field hypotheses before applying that theorem.
boundary: This is a static integration identity for the specified normalized polar measure and its finite product. It gives no derivative in time, entropy evolution, diffusion existence, or density PDE.
Identifying another supplied measure, gradient, divergence, or model generator with these definitions is a separate application obligation.
The proof derives the required radial regularity from the intrinsic hypotheses. It neither assumes nor asserts that the totalized radial extension is continuous or differentiable at the origin.
All integrals are ordinary finite real integrals. The conclusions include integrability, and no almost-everywhere-in-time or finite-horizon convention is involved.
The zero-dimensional sphere and empty product are included. The proof retains the radial factor \(r^n/r\) on positive radii; it does not replace the exponent by truncated natural subtraction.
The stated regularity is classical C¹/C². No weak-gradient, Sobolev, nonsmooth-weight, or arbitrary-measure extension is claimed.
If \(\rho\) is later called a probability density, its nonnegativity and normalization must be supplied by that application. The present geometric identity does not assert them.
units.reader_note: This applies the product-sphere identity to a scalar weight times the coordinate gradient of a C² function. Proof strategy: Differentiate the joint radial extension; Recover a jointly C¹ tangent gradient; Construct the weighted tangent field; Substitute into the proved product identity.
